---
title: "Quick start"
---

## A session

```text
$ onthesignal data/acquisition_FHZ.mseed
onthesignal 0.1.0 — 3 signal(s) loaded (S1, S2, S3). Type / for the list of commands.
ots> list_sig()
ots> S1.sensitivity = 2.384e-6; S1.unit = "V"      # 40 V p-p / 2**24 counts
ots> S1.print()
ots> noise(S1, remove_mains=True)                  # results table
ots> /noise_dsp S1                                 # form with defaults, then figure
ots> /dynamic S2                                   # SINAD, ENOB, SFDR, THD, SNR + figures
ots> /report                                       # report.qmd + figures
ots> S3.sensitivity = 1.59e-9; S3.unit = "m/s"     # 1 / (1500 V/(m/s) × 419430 counts/V)
ots> lnm(S3)
ots> /ai is the noise of S3 below the NLNM?
```

## Two ways to type a command

| Input | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/` command | `/noise S1 fmax=50 remove_mains=true` | without parameters, a form asks for them (Enter keeps the default); `--defaults` skips the form |
| Python | `noise(S1, fmax=50)` | full Python: variables, loops, `S3 = S1 + S2`, `r["rms"]` |

Analyses return a **result**: `r = noise(S1)`, then `r["rms"]`, `r["dr"]`, `r.to_text()`,
`r.save("r.json")`, `r.plot()`.

## Signals

```python
S1.print()                 # every attribute and basic statistics
S1.title = "Shorted input" # title shown in figures, list_sig() and reports (default: file name)
S1.show()                  # time series (matplotlib window)
S2 = 2 * S1                # new signal, amplitude doubled
S4 = S1 + S3               # sum on the common time window (interpolated if needed)
S5 = S1.slice(10, 70)      # seconds 10 to 70
S6 = make_sine(7.3, ratio=0.9, bits=24)   # test sine (see "Test signals")
S1.lnm()                   # same as lnm(S1)
list_sig()                 # table of the signals
```

Signals assigned to a variable are registered in the session under that name; deleting the
variable (`del S4`) removes the signal.
